clue.text: Not showing any development? That's inappropriate

parts.note: UN is the common prefix meaning not
becoming means coming into being, developing into something

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a lack of progress is unseemly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as UN-BECOMING: not becoming, i.e. not developing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbecoming behaviour is unsuitable or improper for the person or occasion.

clue.text: Discovers request in a French document

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside another

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript
ask means request

explanation.surface: A request in a French paper uncovers something.
explanation.walkthrough: Discovers reads as finds, but here it means reveals, taking a disguise off.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmask is to expose or reveal, finding out who someone really is.

clue.text: Club celebrity entertaining army infantry unit

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest, so one piece contains another

parts.note: a bat is a club for hitting a ball
a lion is a celebrity, as in a literary lion
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A famous figure at a club hosts some soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Club looks like a society, but it is the cricket or baseball bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is a large military unit of several companies.

clue.text: Many pressurise caste to reform

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
to lean upon is to put pressure on

indicators.note: to reform means to reshape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of people push a social group into changing its ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges CASTE to ESACT; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To start behaving better after a spell of bad conduct is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Border resident who takes part in protest?

definitions.meaning: someone living in the Marches, the borderlands of England and Wales
a demonstrator walking in a protest procession

explanation.surface: Someone living near the frontier joins a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marches are the border regions between England and Wales, or England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords and folk of the border regions were so called; so is a demonstrator on a protest walk.

clue.text: In absence of drink, devout person's favourite remedy

parts.note: no means without, in the absence of
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a devout person
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: Without alcohol, a pious person turns to a pet cure.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is NO + ST + RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a pet scheme or quack medicine someone swears by.

clue.text: Film star throwing out old clothes

indicators.note: throwing out tells us to remove a letter from the star's name

parts.note: Greta Garbo, the Swedish-born Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: A screen idol clears out a wardrobe of dated outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing out' removes O from GARBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothing or dress, especially distinctive attire.

clue.text: An old politician and I claim to have been in other place

definitions.text: claim to have been in other place

parts.note: an gives the letter A
LIB is short for Liberal, the old British party

explanation.surface: A retired politician and I insist we were elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other place' also means the House of Lords, a misleading picture for politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea of being somewhere else when a crime was committed.

clue.text: Object of terror making badger suffer

parts.note: to badger is to bug, pester
to bear is to suffer, endure

explanation.surface: A frightening thing makes a burrowing animal miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: badger looks like the animal but is the verb, to pester. 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a thing feared or dreaded, originally a hobgoblin.

clue.text: Lacking good fortune in party, individual once slunk out

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a do is a party
own means individual, belonging to oneself

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone down on their luck slips away from a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ONCE SLUNK gives NONESLUCK. The surface suggests someone slinking away from a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in a spell of bad luck or poverty.

clue.text: Admit religion partly goes to bishop's head

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Accepting a faith only halfway goes to a prelate's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's tall ceremonial headdress sits on the head, so it is what goes there.

clue.text: Taking a break, or going in for refurbishment

indicators.note: going in tells us one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: resting means having a rest, taking a break

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to rest or get busy doing up the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; the surface reads like someone choosing between a rest and a renovation.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoring, as a noun of action, is renovation, bringing something back to good condition.

clue.text: Main front man needed to control drift?

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea
an anchor is the presenter fronting a broadcast

explanation.surface: A lead presenter is required to keep a programme from wandering.
explanation.walkthrough: Main as 'the sea' is a crossword convention; capitalised at the start, it looks like an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A drogue streamed from a boat to slow it and hold its head to the wind reduces drift.

clue.text: Sort of art local has no time for

indicators.note: has no tells us to remove a letter from the word for local

parts.note: a native is a local inhabitant

explanation.surface: A local resident cannot spare a moment for a certain artistic genre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' takes T out of NATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive art is the untrained, simple style of painters like Henri Rousseau.

clue.text: Captain's jumper

definitions.meaning: a ship's master or a team leader

explanation.surface: A ship's master owns a knitted pullover.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper looks like the British word for a sweater, but it is one who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's commander is called this, and so is anyone who hops lightly.

clue.text: A German chap coming to the fore as boss

indicators.note: coming to the fore puts the word for chap at the front of the other pieces

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man from Germany rises to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager is the person in charge of staff, a boss.

clue.text: Country's university team represented in sports festival

indicators.note: in tells us pieces go inside another

parts.note: a gala is a sporting festival, like a swimming gala

indicators.note: represented means presented afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A college team turns out for a national sports meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of TEAM gives ATEM. A gala here is a sports meet, as in a British swimming gala.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a Central American republic.

clue.text: Another word for wrongdoing, say, by old corporal

indicators.note: say tells us a word is spoken, giving letters that sound alike

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing
Corporal Nym is a soldier in Shakespeare's Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: An old soldier is looking for a different term for misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns SIN into SYN. NYM is Shakespeare's Corporal Nym. 'for' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym is a different term with the same meaning.

clue.text: One betrays somebody who may know what's in store for her

definitions.meaning: an informer, from the slang shop meaning inform on

definitions.text: somebody who may know what's in store for her
definitions.meaning: a customer who knows what a shop stocks

explanation.surface: A traitor who can foresee her fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's in store' looks like the future, but it is the stock of a shop. To shop someone is British slang for to inform on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls an informer this; so is a customer buying goods.

clue.text: Crazy time to imbibe one sort of wine

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: to imbibe means to drink in, so one piece takes another inside

parts.note: an era is a period of time
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A madcap moment for drinking a particular wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy time' looks like one idea, but Crazy and time give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese island of that name.

clue.text: E.g. Chiron — first to appear in nearly 100 years

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside another
nearly says to drop the last letter of the word for 100 years

parts.note: a century is a hundred years

indicators.note: first to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A mythical figure is said to show up for the first time in almost a hundred years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts CENTURY to CENTUR; 'first to' takes A from 'appear'; 'in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiron was the wise half-man, half-horse of Greek myth who tutored Achilles.

clue.text: MC's equal, having dropped a point

indicators.note: having dropped means one letter slips down to a later place

parts.note: a compeer is an equal, a peer

explanation.surface: A host's peer has lost a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having dropped' moves an E (a point of the compass) lower in COMPEER, giving the answer. Point looks like a score lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere introduces acts, a host or master of ceremonies.

clue.text: Give seat back to person standing

definitions.text: Give seat back to person standing

parts.words: Give seat back to person standing
parts.note: reads like offering a chair to someone on their feet, but means returning a candidate to parliament

explanation.surface: A polite passenger offers their seat to someone standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Standing means standing for election, and a seat is a parliamentary seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters return a sitting member, giving the candidate the seat once more.

clue.text: Kilns originally situated amidst grain

indicators.note: amidst tells us one piece sits in the middle of another

parts.note: oats are a cereal grain

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Drying ovens were first built among the cereal fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives S, and 'amidst' puts it inside OATS. Oast houses are the hop-drying kilns of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasts are the kilns used to dry hops, especially in south-east England.

clue.text: Note about first of planes about to take off

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece holds another

parts.note: so (or soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: first of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: of can mean about, as in to speak of

explanation.surface: A remark about aircraft getting ready for take-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The two abouts do different jobs: one surrounds, one gives letters. Take off looks like flight but means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoof is a parody, and to spoof is to mimic someone humorously.

clue.text: A big fuss connected with mother's craftwork

indicators.note: connected with joins two parts, putting the mother first

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
making a scene is causing a big fuss

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a mother's handicrafts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'connected with' links A SCENE to DAM, which comes first. A dam is a mother, especially of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene work is metal inlaid or etched with decorative patterns, an ornamental craft.

clue.text: Ban student's aid in translation test

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a prose is a school exercise translating into a foreign language
a crib is a literal translation students use

explanation.surface: Teachers forbid study notes during a language exam.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a prose is a passage for translation into a foreign language, and a crib is a literal translation.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to forbid or outlaw.

clue.text: Authoritative order, as accepted in this country by English

indicators.note: accepted in tells us a piece goes inside the others

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, from the British paper's point of view

explanation.surface: A decree is approved throughout Britain and England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. A ukase was originally a decree of the Russian tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was an edict of the Russian tsar, so any arbitrary decree.

clue.text: Fault producing disagreement

definitions.meaning: a geological crack or split in rock

explanation.surface: A mistake leads to a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Fault looks like blame, but it is the geological sense, a break in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift is both a crack in the earth and a breach between people.

clue.text: Special UK-USA rate includes right fare from Germany

indicators.note: includes tells us one piece takes another inside it
special here means specially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trade agreement on air fares between Britain and America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' rearranges UKUSARATE into SAUEKRAUT, and 'includes' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled shredded cabbage is a famous German dish.
